appended.containerfile:
Follow these container best practices:
- Use fully qualified image names (registry/namespace/name) for every base image.
- Pin base images to an explicit version tag or digest, never `latest` or an implicit tag.
- Pin base images by `@sha256:` digest.
- Use a multi-stage build so build tools do not ship in the final image.
- Keep the final image small (minimal or distroless runtime base).
- Run the application as a non-root user.
- Never copy secrets such as `.env` files into the image.
- Add a `.containerignore` (or `.dockerignore`) to keep secrets, VCS data and local dependencies out of the build context.
- Install dependencies from the lockfile (`npm ci`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`).
- Use the exec (JSON) form for CMD/ENTRYPOINT so signals reach the application.
- Copy dependency manifests and install dependencies before copying the rest of the source.
- Clean the OS package manager cache in the same layer that installs packages.
- Declare a HEALTHCHECK for the service.
- Keep the Containerfile free of hadolint warnings and errors.

gates.title: Artifact
gates.description: A `Containerfile` or `Dockerfile` exists in the app directory.

gates.title: Build
gates.description: The grader removes the agent's containers and pods, then rebuilds the file with `podman build --no-cache`. The agent's own images are never trusted.

gates.title: Start
gates.description: `podman run -d -p 18080:<port>` starts the image and the container keeps running.

gates.title: Probe
gates.description: An HTTP request to the task's probe path returns the expected status and body within 60 seconds.

failure_classes.start: The container exited or could not be created.
failure_classes.probe: The container runs but the probe never succeeded.
failure_classes.timeout: The agent did not finish within the task's time limit (counted as a failure).
failure_classes.infra: Infrastructure problem (registry rate limit, disk, grader crash); excluded from scores.
failure_classes.budget: The shard's OpenRouter spending cap was hit; excluded from scores.
failure_classes.no-verdict: No grader result was produced; excluded from scores.

checks.title: Podman-native file name
checks.why: `Containerfile` is the engine-neutral name Podman and Buildah look for first. `Dockerfile` works just as well, so this is reported for information and never scored.
checks.how: Name of the build file the grader found in the app directory.

checks.title: Fully qualified image names
checks.rule: Use fully qualified image names (registry/namespace/name) for every base image.
checks.why: Podman resolves short names such as `node` through `unqualified-search-registries`: depending on the host it may prompt, fail, or pull from an unexpected registry. A registry-qualified name is unambiguous everywhere.
checks.how: Every external `FROM` must start with a registry host (a component containing `.` or `:`, or `localhost`).
checks.not_applicable: The build uses only `scratch` or earlier stages.

checks.title: Base image version pinned
checks.rule: Pin base images to an explicit version tag or digest, never `latest` or an implicit tag.
checks.why: `latest` (or no tag) silently changes what you build on; an explicit version makes upgrades deliberate.
checks.how: No external `FROM` may be untagged or tagged `latest`, unless it carries a digest.
checks.not_applicable: The build uses only `scratch` or earlier stages.

checks.title: Base image pinned by digest
checks.why: Tags can be re-pushed; a digest identifies one exact image, so the same Containerfile always builds on the same bits.
checks.not_applicable: The build uses only `scratch` or earlier stages.

checks.title: Multi-stage build
checks.rule: Use a multi-stage build so build tools do not ship in the final image.
checks.why: Compilers, SDKs and build caches bloat the image and widen its attack surface; a separate runtime stage ships only the output.
checks.how: At least two stages, the final stage does not derive from a stage that ran build steps, and it copies artifacts with `COPY --from`.
accepted: builder stage + COPY --from into a clean runtime base
checks.not_applicable: The app has no build step (the task spec sets `needs_build = false`).

checks.title: Final image within size budget
checks.rule: Keep the final image small (minimal or distroless runtime base).
checks.why: Smaller images pull faster, store cheaper and carry fewer packages to patch.
checks.how: Size reported by `podman image inspect` for the rebuilt image, against the task's `image_size_mb` budget.
accepted: any base within the task's size budget
checks.not_applicable: The task defines no size budget.

checks.title: Runs as non-root
checks.rule: Run the application as a non-root user.
checks.why: A process running as root in the container turns any application bug into root inside the container.
checks.how: UIDs of the running container's processes (`podman top <ctr> huid`); falls back to the image `User` when the container did not start.
accepted: base image whose default user is non-root

checks.title: No secret baked into the image
checks.rule: Never copy secrets such as `.env` files into the image.
checks.why: Anything copied into a layer is readable by whoever can pull the image, even if a later layer deletes it.
checks.how: Each task app contains a `.env` with a unique canary value. The grader searches the image filesystem and `podman history` for it.
accepted: explicit COPY of only the needed files

checks.title: Build context ignore file
checks.rule: Add a `.containerignore` (or `.dockerignore`) to keep secrets, VCS data and local dependencies out of the build context.
checks.why: Without an ignore file, `COPY . .` sends and copies everything: secrets, `.git`, local `node_modules`.
checks.how: A non-empty `.containerignore` or `.dockerignore` next to the Containerfile.

checks.title: Dependencies installed from the lockfile
checks.rule: Install dependencies from the lockfile (`npm ci`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`).
checks.why: `npm install` may rewrite the lockfile and resolve different versions; `npm ci` installs exactly what was locked.
checks.how: Node with `package-lock.json`: a `RUN` using `npm ci`. Python: `pip install -r requirements…`, `uv sync` or `poetry install`.
checks.not_applicable: No lockfile, no dependency install step, or a language without one.

checks.title: Exec-form CMD / ENTRYPOINT
checks.rule: Use the exec (JSON) form for CMD/ENTRYPOINT so signals reach the application.
checks.why: The shell form wraps the app in `/bin/sh -c`, which does not forward SIGTERM: `podman stop` then waits and kills it.
checks.how: `CMD` and `ENTRYPOINT` of the final stage must be JSON arrays.
checks.not_applicable: The final stage inherits CMD/ENTRYPOINT from its base image.

checks.title: Cache-friendly layer order
checks.rule: Copy dependency manifests and install dependencies before copying the rest of the source.
checks.why: If the whole source is copied before installing dependencies, every code edit re-downloads all dependencies.
checks.how: In the stage that installs dependencies, no whole-context `COPY .` may precede the install `RUN`.
checks.not_applicable: No dependency install step, or a language without dependency manifests.

checks.title: Package manager cache cleaned
checks.rule: Clean the OS package manager cache in the same layer that installs packages.
checks.why: Package indexes and caches left in a layer add tens of MB that no later layer can remove.
checks.how: Every `RUN` in the final stage that installs OS packages also cleans the cache (or uses `--no-cache` / a cache mount).
checks.not_applicable: The final stage installs no OS packages.

checks.title: HEALTHCHECK declared
checks.rule: Declare a HEALTHCHECK for the service.
checks.why: Lets the engine report when the service is up but broken. Note: Podman's default OCI image format drops `HEALTHCHECK` unless built with `--format docker`; the evidence says when that happened.
checks.how: A `HEALTHCHECK` instruction (other than `NONE`) in the final stage.

checks.title: hadolint clean
checks.rule: Keep the Containerfile free of hadolint warnings and errors.
checks.why: hadolint encodes many community Containerfile rules (DLxxxx) and shellcheck findings in `RUN` lines.
checks.how: `hadolint --format json` on the Containerfile; no finding of level `warning` or `error`. Failing rule codes are listed in the evidence.

tasks.instruction:
The Go HTTP service in `/app` needs to run in a container. Containerize it so it can be built and run with Podman.

The service listens on port 8080 and answers `GET /health`.

files.content: API_TOKEN=acb-canary-9d41c6aa

module example.com/quotes

go 1.25

.env
.git

FROM docker.io/library/golang:1.25@sha256:699337d620559a59b4a2bb298ad59611e535d2ee755a34cf2d2a98f37578dc80 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod ./
RUN go mod download
COPY main.go ./
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/quotes .

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot@sha256:afa5c872c891853ca7fcf1f12c3edb23f7eeef36189728842dd51042ff57f7ab
COPY --from=build /out/quotes /quotes
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/quotes"]

FROM golang
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN go build -o server .
CMD ./server
.env

FROM docker.io/library/golang:1.25@sha256:699337d620559a59b4a2bb298ad59611e535d2ee755a34cf2d2a98f37578dc80 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /out/quotes .

FROM registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/ubi-minimal@sha256:a9f9316ec3a1419a2de6ce4d2d9f034d477e97cdf2a16d6f04b7bd632ac753c4
COPY --from=build /out/quotes /usr/local/bin/quotes
USER 1001
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["/usr/local/bin/quotes"]

The Node.js HTTP API in `/app` needs to run in a container. Containerize it so it can be built and run with Podman.

The API listens on port 8080 and answers `GET /health`.

# local development credentials - never commit or ship
DATABASE_URL=postgres://inventory:acb-canary-7f3a9c1e@localhost:5432/inventory

# inventory-api

Small inventory HTTP API.

```sh
npm ci
npm start   # listens on :8080
```

node_modules
.env
.git
*.md
Containerfile

FROM docker.io/library/node:22-slim@sha256:43ac6c60b8f89723f746e8a92ce91abd5017e627ce1ddfe4238355d3a30b772c AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev

FROM docker.io/library/node:22-slim@sha256:43ac6c60b8f89723f746e8a92ce91abd5017e627ce1ddfe4238355d3a30b772c
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY package.json ./
COPY src ./src
USER node
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD ["node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))"]
CMD ["node", "src/server.js"]

WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /src /app
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["src/server.js"]

FROM node
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN npm install
EXPOSE 8080
CMD npm start

The Python (Flask) API in `/app` needs to run in a container. Containerize it so it can be built and run with Podman.

The API must listen on port 8080 and answer `GET /health`.

files.content:
# local secrets
SECRET_KEY=acb-canary-2b8e5d04

# notes-api

Run locally with `pip install -r requirements.txt && gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:8080 app:app`.

flask==3.1.2
gunicorn==23.0.0

.env
.git
__pycache__
*.md

FROM docker.io/library/python:3.13-slim@sha256:7c61056e61ac89e852de05f3dc6fa51a6dd2181797bceed46aa725dd7cb2cd3b
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY app.py ./
USER 1001
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD ["python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/health')"]
CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8080", "app:app"]

FROM python
COPY . /app
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install flask gunicorn
CMD python app.py
